chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:

Concerning a man who dies while women are with him and there is no man with them, he عليه السلام said: They should pour water over him from behind the garment, wrap him in his shrouds from beneath the covering, perform salat over him in a row, and place him in his grave. And a woman who dies among men while there is no woman with them, he عليه السلام said: They should pour water from behind the garment, wrap her in her shrouds, perform salat, and bury her.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the reports we presented earlier, because we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation. We only prohibited a woman from washing a man when she directly handles his body; but if she merely pours water over him, then there is no harm in it and there is merit in it. As for the woman, it has also been narrated that it is permissible for men to wash from her those parts they were permitted to look at among her visible features: the face and the hands; this indicates that.

key_terms.الْوَجْهَ وَالْيَدَيْنِ: the face and hands, the parts permitted to be seen
key_terms.مِنْ خَلْفِ الثَّوْبِ: from behind a garment, without direct bodily contact
key_terms.نِسْوَةٌ: women present with the deceased man
key_terms.يُصَلِّينَ عَلَيْهِ: they perform funeral salat over him

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a man or woman dies in travel and only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings for handling the deceased when only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present. It states that water may be poured over the body from behind a garment, the deceased may be shrouded, funeral salat performed, and burial completed, while later juristic clarification explains this as recommended in such circumstances and not as direct bodily washing.
